# catches: a test file that trivially passes (e.g. asserts nothing meaningful) instead
#          of genuinely failing against the throwing stub. Scoped via --filter to THIS
#          task's own new tests only (#193) - never the whole project, which would also
#          run pre-existing HtmlDiagramRendererTests that must stay green.
$ws = $env:GUARDRAILS_WORKSPACE
$proj = Join-Path $ws "tests/Guardrails.Core.Tests/Guardrails.Core.Tests.csproj"

$output = & dotnet test $proj -c Release --nologo --filter "FullyQualifiedName~Render_With" 2>&1
$exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
Write-Output ($output -join "`n")

if ($exitCode -eq 0) {
    Write-Output "---"
    Write-Output "The new tests passed against the stub - they must FAIL until 02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer lands the real behavior. Either the stub is not actually throwing/incomplete, or the tests are not exercising the new behavior."
    exit 1
}

$ranAtLeastOne = $output | Select-String -Pattern "Passed:\s*\d+,\s*Failed:\s*[1-9]"
if (-not $ranAtLeastOne) {
    Write-Output "---"
    Write-Output "Expected at least one failing test matching --filter FullyQualifiedName~Render_With, but none ran or none failed as expected. Check the filter matches the new test names."
    exit 1
}

exit 0

# catches: a test file that does not compile - a non-zero dotnet test exit would
#          otherwise look identical to a genuine TDD red (compiles, fails).
$ws = $env:GUARDRAILS_WORKSPACE
$proj = Join-Path $ws "tests/Guardrails.Core.Tests/Guardrails.Core.Tests.csproj"

$output = & dotnet build $proj -c Release --nologo 2>&1
$exitCode = $LASTEXITCODE
Write-Output ($output -join "`n")

if ($exitCode -ne 0) {
    Write-Output "---"
    Write-Output "Guardrails.Core.Tests does not compile - the new test file and/or stub has a build error."
    exit 1
}

exit 0

content.content: 1 using System.Text.Encodings.Web; 2 using System.Text.Json; 3 4 namespace Guardrails.Core.Graph; 5 6 /// 7 /// Renders the local-viewing companion to diagram.md: a self-contained 8 /// diagram.html that displays the SAME Mermaid DAG with pan / zoom / fullscreen, so a 9 /// large task+guardrail graph is actually navigable on disk (GitHub renders diagram.md 10 /// but offers no navigation). Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its source-sha256 11 /// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33). 12 /// 13 /// 14 /// 15 /// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a 16 /// <script type="text/plain"> element and read back via textContent — never 17 /// interpolated into a JS string. This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a 18 /// backtick, ${, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <script> element's 19 /// content is "raw text" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte. 20 /// This is safe because HTML-escapes every label (so < 21 /// becomes <), meaning the source can never contain </script>. 22 /// 23 /// 24 /// The source-sha256 provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before 25 /// <!doctype html>) so the same \A-anchored reader that validates 26 /// diagram.md validates this file too (graph --check). A comment before the 27 /// doctype does not trigger quirks mode. 28 /// 29 /// 30 /// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs 31 /// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the 32 /// LOCAL artifact; diagram.md remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets) 33 /// is a possible follow-up. 34 /// 35 /// 36 /// Legend overlay. A corner-anchored #legend <div> 37 /// (position: fixed), mirroring the existing #bar/#hint overlay divs, renders 38 /// 's content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native 39 /// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN — 40 /// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra "task" overlapping the real DAG — so 41 /// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from 42 /// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on source-sha256. 43 /// 44 /// 45 /// Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 46 /// superseded, issue #235). A Mermaid click directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster 47 /// element (upstream limitation; see remarks), and the first fix 48 /// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre 49 /// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container 50 /// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail 51 /// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER mermaid.render resolves: for every 52 /// g.cluster element whose id starts with task_, compute a full-width band from the 53 /// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its .cluster-label's bottom edge (Mermaid 54 /// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION 55 /// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and 56 /// append a real <a href="..." target="_blank"><rect fill="transparent"></a> 57 /// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its 58 /// background <rect> then its .cluster-label group, so appending puts the 59 /// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text 60 /// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely 61 /// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's g.cluster — the overlay can never 62 /// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data 63 /// this script needs () is embedded as a small JSON 64 /// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a 65 /// <script type="application/json"> element read back via textContent (same 66 /// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping 67 /// hazards). 68 /// 69 /// 70 /// Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject 71 /// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow). Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title 72 /// <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled mermaid@11.4.1's plain 73 /// flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width = 200 default, 74 /// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout 75 /// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a 76 /// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines 77 /// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned 78 /// directly below.
